clues: This town sits on the Atlantic coast of Argentina. It lies east of a larger city called Bahía Blanca.
Its summer air stays milder than at other beach towns. A sea breeze cools it, and the sea water itself is warmer.
A man named Esteban Dufaur bought this seaside land in 1879. That purchase is why the town exists at all.
This is the only place in Argentina with this trick. The sun rises and sets over the sea.
Look for the Hotel de Madera in this town. It was built with lumber saved from a shipwreck.
